first.rationale:
Two of the three current symptoms (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are funnel-health problems, and the third (competitor entry pricing) is the one where the obvious response — promotional pricing — most threatens the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, since discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are exactly the cohort most likely to churn or repeat-discount. So my default is the friction fix: simplify_onboarding, supported by memory_86 and reinforced by memory_31 and memory_91, which point at the same upstream cause.

But the inherited records are consolidated summaries, and consolidation strips caveats. Every one of these memories is stated in proxy terms: memory_86 reports completion rates and time-to-value, memory_31 reports first-week activation, memory_91 reports week-one engagement. None of them reports revenue retained at 90 days or qualified-revenue quality. It is entirely possible that shortening onboarding raised completion by removing steps that were doing real qualification work — filtering, expectation-setting, data collection that later drove value — in which case the lift is a metric artifact and the downstream cost is invisible in the summary. That is the specific failure mode I am guarding against, so I am spending my first pull on memory_86 to see whether the original record measured anything past the completion event, and whether the population was comparable to today's.

Second pull goes to memory_73 rather than to another onboarding memory, because promotional_pricing is the live alternative under direct competitive pressure and the one I would be wrong to dismiss on summary alone. "Strong acquisition and revenue lift" is the phrasing most likely to conceal a short measurement window. If the archive shows durable retained revenue on the discounted cohort, that materially changes my ranking; if it shows a 30-day acquisition spike, I can rule it out with confidence instead of by prejudice. Verifying the two memories I disagree about is worth more than verifying two that already agree.

Standard experiment, not broad rollout: three simultaneous shifts mean the environment has moved since day 52, so prior effect sizes should be treated as directional, not as estimates. I will instrument on downstream qualified revenue and 60-to-90-day retention, not completion rate, so that a proxy win that destroys value is detectable rather than self-confirming. If memory_86's source turns out to lack any downstream measurement, I drop to a guarded test rather than proceeding at planned scale.
